rationale: This is the archive leader (IncrementalProfitConversion) with WINSOR swapped for IND_ZSCORE on the second leg — a normalization change with a thin economic story rather than a new mechanism, and one that also removes outlier control from a difference-of-deltas ratio, so it reads as the cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

Extending the conversion comparison to a three-year horizon is a substantive persistence-versus-timing test rather than a re-parameterization, the expression correctly matches the stated sign, and the coverage concern is explicitly diagnosed against the earlier five-year construct.

Swapping the gross-profit increment for the net-income increment is a single-input measurement test that is internally consistent and economically arguable, but it is a modest perturbation of the leader and is partly mechanical since the working-capital change is itself embedded in net income, which risks a built-in offset rather than an independent benchmark.

Applying a persistence count to the profit-versus-working-capital increment criterion is a genuinely different construction from the two prior streak signals (which counted raw or sales-scaled accrual declines), the indicator direction matches the positive expected sign, and the discreteness risk is correctly identified and mitigated by the continuous profitability anchor — though the weak alpha of the earlier abnormal-accrual streak tempers expectations.

As a diagnostic ablation the logic is sound and clearly stated, but as a standalone signal it is simply an additive stack of three separately published effects (gross profitability, working-capital accruals, gross-profit growth) with no new mechanism, so it is close to a rediscovery and its most likely outcome is a modest known-factor blend.

This mechanically splices two archived signals using a gating template already used in roughly a dozen archive entries, and the two legs are partly redundant by construction — the profit increment already falls when sales stall — so the "independence test" framing does not disguise that this is incremental stacking within a saturated design family.
